```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
from rse_workbench.helpers import show_submitit_job
from rse_workbench.build_install import install_in_container

```


Now that the project has been defined, the platform
decided on, and the project-specific dependencies have been
defined, it's time to build the final SIF and install the project environment.

We're going to build the final read-only SIF through Slurm 
so Singularity has node-local temporary space and enough memory.
Here's how you build an SBATCH job with `submitit` to build the SIF:

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
import submitit
from pathlib import Path
import os

executor = submitit.AutoExecutor(folder=str(SUBMITIT_DIR / "%j"))
executor.update_parameters(
    timeout_min=SLURM_HOURS * 60,
    slurm_partition=SLURM_PARTITION,
    mem_gb=float(SLURM_MEM.rstrip("G")),
    cpus_per_task=SLURM_CPUS,
    slurm_job_name=f"build-{PROJECT_NAME}-container",
    mail_user=SLURM_EMAIL
)
```

The build function takes the Singularity definition file and an installation
string and builds the SIF. It returns the job ID for tracking.

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
job = executor.submit(build_container, SINGULARITY_DEF, SINGULARITY_SIF)
job.job_id
```

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
result = show_submitit_job(job)
if result is not None:
    print(result)

```

The final install function runs inside the built SIF, binds the project as `/work`,
activates Spack, installs the Spack layer, then runs `rv sync` to
install the project dependencies. It fails loudly if any required
step fails.

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: keep
INSTALL_RUNTIME_COMMAND = r"""
set -euo pipefail

df -h /tmp /work

. /opt/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh
cd /work

spack env activate -d .
spack concretize --force
spack install --deprecated --fail-fast -j8 --no-checksum

rv sync
"""
```

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
job = executor.submit(
    install_in_container,
    project_dir=PROJECT_DIR,
    singularity_sif=SINGULARITY_SIF,
    runtime_command=INSTALL_RUNTIME_COMMAND
)
job.job_id
```

```{python}
#| sorting-hat: remove
result = show_submitit_job(job)
if result is not None:
    print(result)
```

```{python}
print(result['message'][1])
```

When it's time to work on the project, you'll launch
a container with a specific runtime command to
run a VSCode tunnel in a container, with your
project bound to `/work`. The runtime command will 
also activate the project Spack environment and 
install/update project dependencies as needed.

```{python}
runtime_command = [
    "export SPACK_DISABLE_LOCAL_CONFIG=true",
    ". /opt/spack/share/spack/setup-env.sh",
    "cd /work",
    "spack env activate -d .",
    "spack concretize",
    "spack install --deprecated --fail-fast -j12 --no-checksum",
    "rv sync || true",
    f"code tunnel --accept-server-license-terms --name {PROJECT_NAME}-vscode",
]
runtime_command
```

We can write the runtime command to our project-local 
`launch.sh` script. We'll use `simple_slurm`
for this. First, set the job params:

```{python}
from simple_slurm import Slurm

mem = {
    "small": "4G",
    "medium": "8G",
    "big": "32G",
}

n_hours = 4
n_cpus = 12

slurm = Slurm(
    job_name=f"launch-{PROJECT_NAME}-container", 
    cpus_per_task=n_cpus, 
    mem=mem["big"], 
    time=f"0{n_hours}:00:00", 
    partition="hsph",
    mail_user="aaaapr3lk7gfdswioulcmvi3te@harvard.org.slack.com",
    output=str(PROJECT_DIR / "slurm" / "launch" / "logs" / "launch-%j.out"),    
    error=str(PROJECT_DIR / "slurm" / "launch" / "logs" / "launch-%j.err")
)

print(slurm)

slurm.add_cmd("set -o errexit -o nounset -o pipefail")
```

Next, set the project level variabless

```{python}
slurm.add_cmd(f"PROJECT_DIR=${{PROJECT_DIR}}")
slurm.add_cmd(f"SIF=${{PROJECT_DIR}}/.devcontainer/Singularity.sif")
slurm.add_cmd(f"CONTAINER_HOME=${{PROJECT_DIR}}/.container-home")
slurm.add_cmd(f"mkdir -p ${{PROJECT_DIR}}/slurm/launch/logs")
slurm.add_cmd(f"mkdir -p ${{CONTAINER_HOME}}")
slurm.add_cmd(f"cd ${{PROJECT_DIR}}")
```

Next, add some logging to the launch script:

```{python}
slurm.add_cmd("""
echo "================ Slurm tunnel test ================"
echo "Date:         $(date)"
echo "Host:         $(hostname)"
echo "User:         $(whoami)"
echo "Job ID:       ${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
echo "Project:      ${PROJECT_DIR}"
echo "SIF:          ${SIF}"
echo "Home:         ${CONTAINER_HOME}"
echo "Tunnel:       ${TUNNEL_NAME}"
echo "==================================================="

module purge
""")
```

Finally, the runtime command:

```{python}
slurm.add_cmd(r"singularity exec --no-home --bind ${PROJECT_DIR}:/work ${SIF} bash --noprofile --norc -lc '" + " && ".join(runtime_command) + "'")
```

```{python}
print(slurm)
```

And we write this to file:

```{python}
LAUNCH_SCRIPT = PROJECT_DIR / "slurm" / "launch" / "launch_container.sh"

with open(LAUNCH_SCRIPT, "w") as f:
    script = slurm.script(shell="bash")
    f.write(script)
    
LAUNCH_SCRIPT.chmod(0o755)
```

```{python}
Path(LAUNCH_SCRIPT).exists()
```
